## Problem

`gitutil.run_git_bounded` runs git through `gitutil.run_git` → `subprocess.run(..., timeout=...)`. When the bound expires, CPython SIGKILLs only the direct `git` process (`process.kill()` then `wait()`). That causes two problems:

- The git process cannot run its signal cleanup. `git fetch` registers a handler that removes its `objects/pack/pack-*.keep` file on signal, and SIGKILL bypasses it.
- Children such as `index-pack`, `pack-objects`, or the transport's `upload-pack` keep running after their parent dies, reparented to init (or to rebar-mcp when it is the container's PID 1), outside rebar's write lock.

A `.keep` file excludes its pack from every later repack. Until someone deletes it by hand, that pack is never consolidated.

## Evidence

- Production MCP tickets clone, inspected 2026-11-11: 12 `.keep` files, all reading `fetch-pack <pid> on <container-host>`, dated 2026-09-05 through 2026-09-15 UTC, no fetch running. Removed during the maintenance repair for bug `nickelic-lazuline-gonolek`.
- Local reproduction: a stand-in `git` that held a lock and had a child process, run through a `subprocess.run` timeout, left the lock behind and its child reparented to PID 1. The same stand-in under SIGTERM-first process-group reaping (`rebar._proc.reap_process_group`) cleaned up both.

## Root cause

Only the explicit maintenance step (`gitutil.run_git_reaped`, added by `nickelic-lazuline-gonolek`) launches git as its own process group and reaps the group. Every other bounded git call reaches `subprocess.run`'s parent-only kill through one seam: `gitutil.run_git(..., timeout=...)`. Callers: `run_git_bounded` (sync/push fetch+merge+push, store commits via `event_commit_git._run_git`, `run_git_write`, snapshot `git_fetch`, fsck health, completion candidate, link revert, store usability) and the direct `run_git(..., timeout=...)` sites (`freshness`, `fsck_repair`, `link_revert`, reconciler `git_adapter`, code-review `assemble`).

## Plan

Fix it at that one seam, so every bounded git call is covered without touching callers:

1. `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py`: when `run_git` gets a `timeout`, launch git with `start_new_session=True` (POSIX) via `subprocess.Popen` and `communicate(input, timeout)`; on `TimeoutExpired` or any interruption call `reap_process_group` (SIGTERM, 5 s grace, then SIGKILL) and re-raise, so `run_git_bounded`'s existing fold to code `124` and every caller's `TimeoutExpired` handling are unchanged. `check`, `capture_output`, `text`, `env`, and `input_data` keep `subprocess.run` semantics. `timeout=None` keeps the plain `subprocess.run` path.
2. `run_git_reaped` (the maintenance step) delegates to `run_git_bounded`, so there is one group-reaping launcher instead of two.
3. Tests that spied on `subprocess.run` for timeout-bounded git calls are retargeted to the new seam (assert the bound is still passed).
4. `docs/concurrency.md` scale-up paragraph and ADR 0051 amendment: one sentence each stating every bounded git child is group-reaped.

No config key, env var, flag, or new lock. `runner=` seams in `push`/`sync` are unchanged (they pass `run_git`, which now reaps).

## File impact

- `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py`
- `tests/unit/test_bounded_git_group_reap.py` (new)
- `tests/unit/test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py` (spy retarget)
- `docs/concurrency.md`, `docs/adr/0051-foreground-git-maintenance-tickets-worktree.md`

## Resolution

Landed as Gerrit 3356, merged `d779ed59793`. The seam is `gitutil._run_in_group`, which takes subprocess.run's keywords. 15 test files that faked `subprocess.run` for bounded git now also patch that seam with the same fake. `test_bounded_git_group_reap.py` fails on the pre-fix code: the `.keep` is left behind.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] When a bounded git child times out, its whole process group is reaped, SIGTERM first, so no git descendant outlives the call.
- [x] A test proves that a bounded fetch interrupted by its bound leaves no `.keep` file and no surviving child process.
- [x] [non-codebase] `make verify` passes on the change.
